summary: Wilhelm Gesenius worked in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at the University of Helmstedt (~1803-1804) and University of Göttingen (~1804-1806), later holding posts at Göttingen (~1806-1809) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1810-1842).

Wilhelm Grube studied sinology and linguistics at Saint Petersburg (1874-1878) under Vasilyev and Schiefner, and at Leipzig (PhD 1878-1880) under von der Gabelentz. He worked at the Asiatic Museum, Ethnological Museum of Berlin, and Humboldt University of Berlin (1884, 1892).
Wilhelm Gundert worked in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Succeeding Karl Florenz, he held a post at the University of Hamburg from approximately 1936 to 1945.

Wilhelm Halbfass was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Vienna (~1962-1963) and Göttingen (~1963-1967). He held posts at Göttingen (~1968-1971), Hamburg (~1972-1973), and the University of Pennsylvania (1982-2000).

Wilhelm Havers worked in linguistics and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (~1913-1915), University of Bern (~1915-1920), University of Breslau (~1920-1928), University of Würzburg (~1928-1937), and University of Vienna (~1937-1953).

Wilhelm K. Essler specialized in philosophy and Indology, studying at the University of Munich (~1960-1966) under Wolfgang Stegmüller and Wilhelm Britzelmayr. He served as Director of the Institute for Philosophy at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1980-2005).

Wilhelm Max Müller worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1883-1885) and the University of Leipzig (~1885-1888), and held a post at the University of Pennsylvania (~1910-1919).

Wilhelm Pertsch was an Indology and Iranian/Central Asian scholar who studied under Albrecht Weber, Rudolf von Roth, and at Tübingen and Berlin. He held posts at Forschungsbibliothek Gotha, Münzkabinett Gotha (1874), and Wissenschaftliche Anstalten auf Schloss Friedenstein (1883).
Wilhelm Printz worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Heinrich Lüders (~1909-1914) and Wilhelm Schulze (~1910-1914).

Wilhelm Rau worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Leipzig under Friedrich Weller and Marburg under Johannes Nobel. He held posts at Goethe University Frankfurt (1955), Marburg (1958-1987), and Leipzig (1992-1993).

Wilhelm Roscher studied at the University of Göttingen (~1835-1838) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1838-1839). He subsequently held posts at Göttingen (~1840-1848), the University of Leipzig (~1848-1894), and Humboldt University of Berlin.

Wilhelm Scherer studied linguistics at Vienna and Berlin under Haupt, Bopp, and Müllenhoff. He held posts at the University of Vienna (1864, 1868-1872), University of Strasbourg (1872), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1877).

Wilhelm Schmidt worked in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1893-1895) and held posts at the University of Vienna (~1921-1938) and the University of Fribourg (~1939-1951).

Wilhelm Schott specialized in sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1823-1826) and later held a post there from approximately 1838 to 1889.

Wilhelm Schulze studied linguistics and Indology at Berlin and Greifswald under Schmidt, Zimmer, Kießling, Kaibel, and Wilamowitz-Moellendorff. He held chairs and posts at Marburg (1892), Göttingen (1895), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1902-1932).
Wilhelm Solf studied Indology at Berlin, Göttingen, Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel, Kiel, and Jena, in addition to gymnasium schooling. He held a post at Kiel University (~1887-1888).
Wilhelm Storck studied under Franz Bopp and Moriz Haupt.

Wilhelm Streitberg studied linguistics and Indology at Leipzig under Brugmann and Windisch, Münster, and Berlin. He held posts at Fribourg (~1889-1898), Leipzig (1898, 1920-1925), Münster (1899), and Munich (1909-1920).

Wilhelm Vatke worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg (~1824-1826), Göttingen (~1826-1827), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1827-1829), where he later held a post from approximately 1834 to 1882.

Wilhelm Wackernagel studied linguistics at Humboldt University of Berlin (1824-1827) under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh. He held posts at the Pädagogium Basel (~1833-1835) and the University of Basel (1833, 1835-1869).
